title: Monthly Active User Count
description:
Count the number of **distinct active users** for each calendar month. A user is considered active in a month if they appear at least once in the events table that month.

**Table: events** — `event_id`, `user_id`, `event_date`, `event_type`

Output columns: `month`, `active_users`. Order by `month`.
solution_sql: SELECT DATE_TRUNC('month', event_date)::DATE AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) AS active_users FROM events GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', event_date) ORDER BY month;

test_cases.description: Jan: users 1,2,3 (3 distinct); Feb: users 2,4,5 (3 distinct); Mar: users 1,3,6 (3 distinct)

hints: Use DATE_TRUNC('month', event_date) to group all dates in the same month together.
Use COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) to avoid counting the same user twice within a month.
Cast the result to DATE (::DATE) so the output shows a date rather than a timestamp.
explanation: DATE_TRUNC('month', event_date) truncates each date to the first of its month, enabling month-level grouping. COUNT(DISTINCT user_id) correctly handles users who appear multiple times in a month (e.g., user 2 appears twice in January). Each of the 3 months has 3 unique active users.
